findings.issue_text: Gemfile.lock not updated with new gems (ruby-readability, simple-rss), breaking bundle install --frozen/--deployment

topic_embed.rb:31 — title never validated before import; blank/nil titles can create topics with skip_validations: true (ruby-readability returns nil title)

cook_method: :raw_html bypasses the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline and PostCreator accepts it from any caller with no restriction, introducing an unsanitized-HTML path into the core post pipeline (lib/post_creator.rb:216, app/models/post.rb:131-135)
RSS i.content is inserted with CGI.unescapeHTML and cooked via return raw, gated only by a loose /^https?\:\/\// URL check, allowing untrusted remote HTML into posts (app/models/post.rb:131-135)
Migration default cook_method: 1 maps to :raw_html enum instead of 0, making all posts bypass markdown/sanitization and render raw HTML
External RSS/HTML content is imported into post raw with no sanitization step anywhere in the embed import path
Redis setnx followed by expire is not atomic; crash between calls leaves key with no TTL, permanently blocking that URL's retrieval
sidekiq retry: false on RetrieveTopic failure paths makes lost retrievals silently unrecoverable, causing endless 'loading' reloads
PollFeed uses i.content without nil check; items without content (Atom summary-only) raise NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll run
CGI.unescapeHTML double-decodes already-escaped HTML bodies, corrupting content
Single embeddable_host scalar setting bakes a one-site assumption into the data model instead of a hosts table/feed registry
PollFeed hardwired to exactly one feed URL and one author username rather than a feed registry
topic_embed.content_sha1 is updated via update_column even when revise! fails, letting hash and content drift so updates are permanently lost
Loading sentinel embed page has no error/terminal state; failures cause infinite 30-second reloads hammering embed/best and re-enqueuing jobs
open(url) in TopicRetriever has no timeout, so a hang blocks indefinitely
Check-then-insert on embed_url creates a race between controller job and hourly poll producing duplicate topics/lost updates; should be upsert with optimistic guard
embed.js uses indexOf substring comparison for origin validation, allowing lookalike origins to hijack the iframe messaging channel
feed_key cache key is built but never read; no conditional GET/ETag or item LIMIT, causing hourly full re-parse and unbounded first-run backlog imports
import_remote fetches arbitrary URL with no timeout, size cap, content-type check, or SSRF containment, enabling slow-loris-style worker exhaustion
Controller spec mocks TopicEmbed/TopicView entirely, verifying wiring only and not actual rendering for anonymous users
Migration add_cook_method_to_posts defaults cook_method to 1 (raw_html) instead of 0 (regular), causing all posts to skip the cooking/markdown pipeline and bypass XSS-relevant sanitization
Existing migration create_top_topics edited in place to add force: true, so re-runs will drop and recreate the table, destroying data
disqus:import task removed the --category option and switched to TopicEmbed.import_remote fetching remote content over HTTP, breaking existing scripts and changing import behavior silently
post_revisor.rb save changed to save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]), allowing imported embedded posts to bypass all post validations on revision
Whitespace-only edit to existing migration migrate_word_counts.rb, including stripped trailing newline, polluting the diff

Stored XSS: post.cook with cook_method raw_html returns unsanitized raw feed HTML, and embed view renders it via raw post.cooked; Readability whitelist doesn't strip event handlers like onerror/onload, allowing stored XSS from imported third-party articles/feeds

HTML/attribute injection: topic_embed.rb interpolates url into HTML with only a weak ^https?:// regex check, allowing crafted URLs (e.g. with ' onmouseover=') to inject raw HTML into post body, leading to stored XSS

Reflected XSS: embed.html.erb interpolates client-controlled Referer header into inline JS postMessage call without escaping; ensure_embeddable only validates the host, so attacker-controlled path/query can break out of the JS string
SSRF: open-uri fetches in TopicEmbed and PollFeed follow redirects without host/scheme validation, allowing the embeddable host to redirect the server to internal addresses like 169.254.169.254
Weak origin check in embed.js uses substring matching (indexOf) instead of strict origin equality, potentially allowing suffix/subdomain origin matches when trusting e.data.height
topic_retriever_spec.rb:32-43 stubs retrieved_recently? and only tests dispatch, leaving real throttle logic (setnx/expire, no_throttle staff bypass) untested
No test coverage for the no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) path wired in retrieve_topic.rb:16
poll_feed_spec.rb:31-39 stubs poll_feed itself; real poll_feed body (SimpleRSS parsing, url fallback branch, CGI.unescapeHTML, user lookup, TopicEmbed.import) never executed by tests
post_revisor.rb:85 save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) behavioral change has no test passing skip_validations to revise!
embed_controller_spec.rb:36-42 asserts against mocks instead of verifying Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) with correct embed_url/user_id
topic_embed_spec.rb:39-42 never verifies content_sha1 is updated, so regression to a no-op update_column causing permanent re-revision would go undetected
cook_method migration default of 1 means raw_html, backfilling all existing posts to raw_html so cooked output silently becomes raw markdown
PostCreator never sets cook_method for new posts, so all new posts inherit DB default 1 (raw_html) and are rendered raw
force: true added to create_table :top_topics migration will DROP TABLE and irreversibly destroy existing top_topics data on re-execution
topic_embeds migration creates no foreign keys, allowing dangling topic_id/post_id references that break the embed route when topics/posts are deleted

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile.lock not updated with new gems (ruby-readability, simple-rss), breaking bundle install --frozen/--deployment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile`, and it also updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock` to include both gems (and their dependency `guess_html_encoding`) in the GEM and DEPENDENCIES sections. While `Gemfile.lock` is not shown/updated in this diff, the finding as stated (“Gemfile.lock not updated…”) is not verifiably true from the diff and is contradicted by the updated lockfile that is present (`Gemfile_rails4.lock`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:33 assumes i.content exists on every feed item; RSS items often only have description or neither, causing NoMethodError and killing the hourly poll
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `i.content` is assumed to exist for all RSS items and that many feeds only provide `description` (or nothing), which can cause a NoMethodError/crash. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment and implies the need for a fallback (e.g., to `description`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32-35 assumes Atom semantics for i.id fallback; RSS items without id can produce nil url, raising on the regex check or in TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `url` can become `nil` if both `i.link` and `i.id` are blank. However, this does not raise: `url.blank?` handles `nil`, `nil !~ /.../` is valid in Ruby (it evaluates to `true`), and `TopicEmbed.import` safely returns early because `nil =~ /.../` is `nil` (no exception). The item would be skipped, but the proposed finding’s claim about raising on the regex check or in `TopicEmbed.import` is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub requires Ruby >= 2.1 but the codebase targets Ruby 2.0.x, so i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a call to `i.content.scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, and `String#scrub` is not available on older Rubies. However, the finding’s core premise (“the codebase targets Ruby 2.0.x”) is not established anywhere in this diff (no Ruby version constraint, .ruby-version, gemspec requirement, etc.). Without verifiable evidence from the diff that the runtime Ruby is < 2.1, this is speculative rather than a confirmed defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb uses require_dependency 'nokogiri' instead of require for a third-party gem, risking LoadError/NameError outside Rails dependency-tracking context

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TopicEmbed` is a Rails model (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`) that will be loaded within a Rails environment where `require_dependency` is available. In Rails, `require_dependency` ultimately delegates to `require` and is commonly used to track dependencies for reloading; using it to load a gem like `nokogiri` does not inherently risk `LoadError/NameError` compared to `require`. The claimed “outside Rails dependency-tracking context” scenario isn’t evidenced by this diff, and within Rails this is not a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Digest::SHA1 used in topic_embed.rb without requiring 'digest/sha1', relying on incidental load order

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `app/models/topic_embed.rb` calls `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` but does not `require 'digest/sha1'` (or at least `require 'digest'`). In this diff, `digest/sha1` is only required in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, so other entry points that use `TopicEmbed` (e.g. `TopicRetriever#import_remote` and the updated `disqus.thor` task calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) do not ensure the Digest constant/algorithm is loaded. That makes `TopicEmbed.import` potentially raise `NameError: uninitialized constant Digest` depending on load order/environment, i.e. it relies on incidental requires elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb:4 assumes @topic_view and @topic_view.topic are non-nil on all render paths; empty posts list crashes the embed page

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `@topic_view` is only set when `topic_id` is found; otherwise the action renders the separate `loading` template and does not render `best.html.erb`. Therefore `best.html.erb` is not executed on the nil-`@topic_view` path. Also, when `@topic_view` exists but has an empty `posts` list, the template’s else branch still uses `@topic_view.topic.url`, which should be available given a valid `topic_id` passed to `TopicView.new`. The finding’s claimed crash path (empty posts causing nil dereference) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:33 — `i.content` may be nil for Atom entries with only summary, causing NoMethodError; with retry: false the entire hourly poll silently aborts

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common for some Atom/RSS variants that only provide `summary`/`description`), `i.content` will be nil and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job before processing remaining items. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so this failure will not be retried by Sidekiq (though it would run again on the next scheduled recurrence).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:26 — `feed_key` (Last-Modified/ETag) is dead code; no conditional GET, so all feeds are re-downloaded and re-imported hourly via PostRevisor

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (suggesting intent to track Last-Modified/ETag or similar) but is never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it is dead code. Also, `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no conditional request/caching logic, so the feed will be re-downloaded on every hourly run. However, the finding’s claim that it is “re-imported hourly via PostRevisor” is overstated: `TopicEmbed.import` only calls `PostRevisor` when `content_sha1` changes; otherwise it avoids revising, though it still reprocesses items and does DB lookups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:38-42 — `content_sha1` is updated unconditionally even when `PostRevisor#revise!` returns false, permanently skipping the changed article

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking the return value or whether the post was actually updated. Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (e.g., when `should_revise?` is false), this can record the new SHA1 even though the post content wasn’t revised, causing subsequent polls with the same changed content to be skipped because the stored SHA1 now matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:24-35 — concurrent imports race on the unique embed_url index causing unhandled RecordNotUnique; throttle bypassed by staff

adjudication.rationale: Yes for the first part: `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-insert (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then later `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction). With concurrent callers importing the same URL, both can observe `embed.blank?` and attempt `create!`; the second will hit the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` and raise an unrescued `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or adapter-specific unique violation), causing the job/request to error. The "throttle bypassed by staff" portion is not clearly a defect in this diff (it appears intentional via `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`), but the race/RecordNotUnique issue is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb:8-10 — infinite 30s reload with no failure path when retrieval fails (invalid URL, open() error, blank embed_by_username)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the script unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds. The controller renders this `loading` view whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, after enqueueing `:retrieve_topic`. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., `TopicRetriever` refuses to fetch due to invalid host, `embed_by_username` missing so `fetch_http` returns early, or `open(...)`/network/readability parsing errors prevent creating a `TopicEmbed`), the embed will keep rendering the loading page and reloading forever with no retry limit or failure/timeout path. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js:5-11 — no check that `#discourse-comments` div exists before calling appendChild, causing TypeError on publisher pages missing the div; postMessage resize handshake also unverified

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then `comments.appendChild(iframe)` is called unconditionally. If the embedding script is loaded on a page that does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a TypeError at runtime. There is no guard in the diff to prevent this. (The additional note about postMessage verification is more debatable, but the missing null-check is a concrete defect in the shown code.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test verification for update path: content_sha1 update, no-op re-import not creating revision, and sha-vs-absolutize ordering invariant are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds basic coverage for the update path in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` (“Supports updating the post”), but it does not assert details like `content_sha1` being updated, no-op re-imports avoiding revision, or the relationship between SHA calculation and `absolutize_urls`. However, this is fundamentally a request for more test assertions/coverage rather than a concrete defect introduced by the code: nothing in the diff shows incorrect behavior or failing invariants, only that certain behaviors are not explicitly tested. Missing tests are not, by themselves, a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:31 — title never validated before import; blank/nil titles can create topics with skip_validations: true (ruby-readability returns nil title)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when no existing embed is found it creates the first post/topic via `PostCreator.new(user, title: title, ..., skip_validations: true, ...)` without any guard that `title` is present/non-blank. Since validations are explicitly skipped, a nil/blank `title` coming from `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`opts[:title] || doc.title`) or from RSS (`i.title`) can lead to attempting to create a topic/post with an invalid/missing title (either creating bad data if DB allows it, or raising on DB constraints and aborting the import). This is directly observable from the diff; there is no prior validation of `title` in the shown code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import rewrite removes the --category option and category_id lookup, breaking the documented import workflow and losing category assignment (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-150)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor option `:category` and the entire `category_id` lookup/usage in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`. The import now always calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not accept or pass through any category information (they ultimately call `PostCreator.new(..., title:, raw:, ...)` without `category:`). So there is no longer any way for the Disqus import task to assign imported topics to a specified category, which is a concrete behavioral regression for anyone relying on `--category`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import now routes through TopicEmbed.import_remote fetching full remote HTML, which fails at import time for dead Disqus t[:link] URLs (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-150)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the import no longer creates a topic/post from the Disqus thread data directly; it now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (via open-uri) and parses it with Readability, with no error handling. If `t[:link]` is unreachable/dead/returns an error, `open(url)` will raise (e.g., OpenURI::HTTPError, SocketError), causing the Disqus import task to fail at import time. Previously, the code did not fetch remote HTML at all, so this is a new failure mode introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :top_topics adds force: true to an already-shipped migration, which destroys existing top_topics data on re-run and won't apply to deployed databases (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can destroy any existing `top_topics` data if this migration is ever executed against a DB where the table is present. Additionally, because this is an already-timestamped migration, deployed databases that have already run it will not re-run it, so the change will not take effect there (migration versions prevent re-execution).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated whitespace churn (trailing-space removal, newline at EOF) in an existing migration creates diff noise and merge-conflict risk (db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:4,33)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include unrelated whitespace-only edits in `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` (a trailing-space cleanup near the top and toggling the newline-at-EOF, as indicated by `\ No newline at end of file`). However, this is not a functional/correctness/security defect introduced by the change—it's purely diff noise/style churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is computed but never used, so the 'only import modified feeds' requirement is not enforced and every hourly run re-parses and re-imports all items (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25-27)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (computes a Redis/cache key based on the feed URL) but is never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`. The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item on every run, with no conditional fetch (ETag/Last-Modified) or “only if feed changed” short-circuit. While `TopicEmbed.import` prevents duplicate topics by checking existing `TopicEmbed` rows and comparing `content_sha1`, the finding’s core point—that the computed `feed_key` is unused and there is no “only import when modified” mechanism—is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed re-issues open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and full parses hourly with no conditional-GET, and the promised feed-modified cache key does not exist (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25-27)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job runs hourly and unconditionally does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` inside `poll_feed`, with no use of HTTP conditional headers or any caching to avoid re-downloading/parsing when unchanged. Although a `feed_key` method is defined (intended for caching last-modified/etag or similar), it is never referenced anywhere in the diff, so no “feed-modified” cache key is actually used to gate fetching/parsing. This is a concrete inefficiency/defect visible in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untraceable formatting change (removed blank line after should_revise? guard) bundled with the skip_validations feature (lib/post_revisor.rb:11-14)

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/post_revisor.rb removes a blank line after `return false if not should_revise?` and changes `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. The only “formatting change” mentioned is the removed blank line, which is purely stylistic and not a verifiable defect. Bundling a whitespace change with a functional change may be undesirable review practice, but it is not a bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method: :raw_html bypasses the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline and PostCreator accepts it from any caller with no restriction, introducing an unsanitized-HTML path into the core post pipeline (lib/post_creator.rb:216, app/models/post.rb:131-135)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `Post.cook_methods` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping the normal cooking pipeline (which is where HTML is typically sanitized/normalized). `PostCreator` is updated to set `post.cook_method` directly from `@opts[:cook_method]` with no restriction/whitelisting. The new feed/embed import paths (`TopicEmbed.import` / `PollFeed`) explicitly create posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` from remote RSS/Readability content, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making this an actual unsanitized-HTML rendering path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS i.content is inserted with CGI.unescapeHTML and cooked via return raw, gated only by a loose /^https?\:\/\// URL check, allowing untrusted remote HTML into posts (app/models/post.rb:131-135)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a raw HTML path for posts: Post#cook now returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). PollFeed builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` and explicitly sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` with `skip_validations: true` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, app/models/topic_embed.rb). There is no HTML sanitization of the feed content (String#scrub is encoding repair, not sanitization), and the only check is that the URL starts with http(s). This introduces a straightforward stored-XSS risk: arbitrary remote feed HTML can be stored and then rendered as-is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration default cook_method: 1 maps to :raw_html enum instead of 0, making all posts bypass markdown/sanitization and render raw HTML

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `Post.cook_methods` as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration sets `posts.cook_method` default to `1`. In this codebase, `Enum` values are 1-based (evidenced by the existing `Post.types` enum and Discourse’s historical convention where `post_type` default 1 corresponds to `:regular`). Therefore default `1` maps to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Only imported posts explicitly pass `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` to `PostCreator`. So the claim that "all posts bypass markdown/sanitization" is a misread of the enum mapping and is not verifiably true from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External RSS/HTML content is imported into post raw with no sanitization step anywhere in the embed import path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an embed import path that explicitly bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. In `TopicEmbed.import`, external `contents` (from RSS in `Jobs::PollFeed` via `i.content`/`i.title`, and from `import_remote` via `Readability::Document#content`) are passed to `PostCreator` as `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` causes `return raw`, skipping the normal rendering/cooking filters where sanitization typically happens. Additionally, `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href/src` and does not sanitize HTML. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML from the feed/page is rendered directly. Therefore, external RSS/HTML is imported and displayed without a sanitization step in this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redis setnx followed by expire is not atomic; crash between calls leaves key with no TTL, permanently blocking that URL's retrieval

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two distinct Redis commands; if the process crashes (or loses connectivity) after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will persist without a TTL. That would cause `setnx` to keep returning false on subsequent calls, making `retrieved_recently?` return true indefinitely and permanently throttling retrieval for that embed_url. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sidekiq retry: false on RetrieveTopic failure paths makes lost retrievals silently unrecoverable, causing endless 'loading' reloads

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not set `sidekiq_options retry: false` on `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`. `retry: false` is only added to the *scheduled* `Jobs::PollFeed` job (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). `RetrieveTopic` (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`) has no `sidekiq_options` in this change, so the finding’s premise is incorrect. While the embed loading page does reload every 30s when no topic is found, whether a failed `RetrieveTopic` would be “silently unrecoverable” depends on Sidekiq/Jobs defaults not shown in the diff, so it’s not verifiable from this patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed uses i.content without nil check; items without content (Atom summary-only) raise NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll run

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed iterates `rss.items.each` and unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If an RSS/Atom item has no `content` (i.e., `i.content` is nil), calling `.scrub` on nil will raise `NoMethodError`, which would abort the polling run for the whole feed. There is no fallback to `i.summary`, `i.description`, or an empty string, nor a nil check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML double-decodes already-escaped HTML bodies, corrupting content

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which performs a single HTML-entity decode pass on the feed item content before importing. The diff does not show the content being decoded elsewhere (no second `unescapeHTML`, no evidence `SimpleRSS.parse` already returns an already-decoded string), so the specific claim of a *double*-decode causing corruption is not verifiable from this change. Whether decoding entities is correct depends on feed semantics, but that’s speculative and not a clear defect demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single embeddable_host scalar setting bakes a one-site assumption into the data model instead of a hosts table/feed registry

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a single `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and enforces it in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` by requiring the request referer/URL host to match that one setting. This does create a one-host limitation, but it is not a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the diff—it's an architectural/product choice. Nothing in the diff indicates the feature is meant to support multiple embeddable hosts or that the current behavior is incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed hardwired to exactly one feed URL and one author username rather than a feed registry

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Jobs::PollFeed` that reads `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` and `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` (single-valued settings) and imports items from that configured URL as that configured user. This does mean the implementation supports only one feed and one author at a time, but it is not “hardwired” (it’s configurable) and nothing in the diff indicates that multi-feed/registry support is required. This is a design/feature suggestion rather than a clear defect or correctness/security bug introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.content_sha1 is updated via update_column even when revise! fails, letting hash and content drift so updates are permanently lost

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is updated, the code does:

```rb
revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)
revisor.revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)
embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)
```

`update_column` is executed unconditionally whenever `content_sha1` differs, and the return value of `revise!` is ignored. If `revise!` returns `false` (e.g., `should_revise?` prevents the edit or the update fails without raising), the post content may remain unchanged while `topic_embeds.content_sha1` is advanced. After that, future imports will see matching SHA1 and skip updating, effectively losing subsequent updates. This drift is a direct consequence of the unguarded `update_column` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading sentinel embed page has no error/terminal state; failures cause infinite 30-second reloads hammering embed/best and re-enqueuing jobs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The new `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` contains a `setTimeout` that calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no max retry or error state. If the embed retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch fails or settings prevent import), the iframe will reload forever, repeatedly requesting `/embed/best?embed_url=...` and re-enqueueing `:retrieve_topic` each time. While `TopicRetriever` throttles the *work* to once per 60s via Redis, the controller still enqueues a job per reload, so the “infinite reload + re-enqueue” behavior is a real issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) in TopicRetriever has no timeout, so a hang blocks indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote fetching via `open(uri)` with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options. While `TopicRetriever` doesn’t call `open` directly, it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` without timeouts, and `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` similarly. This can cause the request/job to block for an unbounded time under slow/stalled network conditions (no application-level timeout is set in the code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-insert on embed_url creates a race between controller job and hourly poll producing duplicate topics/lost updates; should be upsert with optimistic guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple concurrent entry points that can create the same embed (EmbedController enqueues RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever.fetch_http -> TopicEmbed.import_remote/import, and scheduled PollFeed -> TopicEmbed.import). TopicEmbed.import performs a classic check-then-insert: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, creates a Post/Topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!`. Although a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` exists, concurrent callers can both see no row and race to `create!`, causing one to raise (RecordNotUnique) and potentially leaving extra work/side effects (e.g., a topic/post created before the failing insert, depending on transaction boundaries inside PostCreator). There is no rescue/ retry / upsert logic, so this is a real concurrency/correctness hazard introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js uses indexOf substring comparison for origin validation, allowing lookalike origins to hijack the iframe messaging channel
feed_key cache key is built but never read; no conditional GET/ETag or item LIMIT, causing hourly full re-parse and unbounded first-run backlog imports

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined to generate a cache key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the job (no Redis read/write, no timestamp comparison). The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` every time it runs (hourly), with no conditional GET headers (ETag/If-Modified-Since) and no explicit item limit. While `TopicEmbed.import` dedupes by `embed_url`, the job still re-downloads/re-parses the whole feed and processes every item each run, and on first run it will attempt to import every item present in the feed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote fetches arbitrary URL with no timeout, size cap, content-type check, or SSRF containment, enabling slow-loris-style worker exhaustion

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, no response size limit, and no content-type validation:

```rb
Doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)
```

This is reachable from background jobs (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) that can be triggered by `EmbedController#best` enqueuing `:retrieve_topic`. Even though `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` restricts the host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the code still allows a slow/unresponsive endpoint on that allowed host (or very large responses) to block Sidekiq workers and exhaust resources. Additionally, `import_remote` itself contains no SSRF/host containment and is also called from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, so containment is not guaranteed by the method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller spec mocks TopicEmbed/TopicView entirely, verifying wiring only and not actual rendering for anonymous users

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s controller spec (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb) does stub/mock TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and TopicView.new, so it tests controller wiring rather than exercising real TopicView creation/rendering. However, that is a test-scope choice, not a verifiable defect/bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the code. The spec still checks anonymous-user wiring by expecting TopicView.new with a nil user. Lack of an integration-style rendering assertion is not, by itself, a concrete problem in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration add_cook_method_to_posts defaults cook_method to 1 (raw_html) instead of 0 (regular), causing all posts to skip the cooking/markdown pipeline and bypass XSS-relevant sanitization

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on an assumption that `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` maps `:regular` to 0 and `:raw_html` to 1. In this codebase, the existing pattern `Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` for `Post.types` strongly suggests a 1-based enum (commonly `:regular` => 1, `:moderator_action` => 2). Under that mapping, the migration’s `default: 1` sets `cook_method` to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`, so posts would continue to go through the normal cooking pipeline unless explicitly set to `raw_html` (as done for RSS imports). There’s no concrete evidence in the diff that the enum is 0-based or that `1` corresponds to `raw_html`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing migration create_top_topics edited in place to add force: true, so re-runs will drop and recreate the table, destroying data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` would drop an existing `top_topics` table if that migration were executed against a DB where the table already exists, Rails will not normally “re-run” an already-applied migration, and a fresh migrate from scratch won’t have the table yet. So the finding’s data-destruction scenario depends on atypical/manual re-execution or a DB already containing the table despite the migration being pending, which is not a direct, verifiable problem introduced by this diff in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus:import task removed the --category option and switched to TopicEmbed.import_remote fetching remote content over HTTP, breaking existing scripts and changing import behavior silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Disqus Thor task option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes all code that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. It also replaces the previous `PostCreator.new(... raw: "[Permalink](...)" ...)` behavior with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which fetches and imports remote content over HTTP. This is a clear, verifiable breaking change to the task’s CLI and behavior with no compatibility shim in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor.rb save changed to save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]), allowing imported embedded posts to bypass all post validations on revision

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change PostRevisor’s `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which means validations can be skipped when the *caller* passes `skip_validations: true` (and TopicEmbed.import does pass that when revising imported content). However, the finding frames this as a defect without showing any path where an end-user can set `skip_validations` or that skipping validations here is unintended. In this diff it appears to be an intentional behavior change to honor an existing option for import/update flows, not a verifiable bug/security issue on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only edit to existing migration migrate_word_counts.rb, including stripped trailing newline, polluting the diff

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb the only substantive changes are whitespace: a line with trailing spaces is normalized ("-  " to "+"), and the file now lacks a trailing newline ("\ No newline at end of file"). This does "pollute the diff" but it does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect in the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: post.cook with cook_method raw_html returns unsanitized raw feed HTML, and embed view renders it via raw post.cooked; Readability whitelist doesn't strip event handlers like onerror/onload, allowing stored XSS from imported third-party articles/feeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to imported content (`absolutize_urls(url, contents)`) derived directly from RSS/Atom (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content` + `CGI.unescapeHTML`, no sanitization) or from `Readability::Document` HTML. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, which for these posts equals the unsanitized `raw` HTML. Therefore attacker-controlled HTML from feeds/articles can be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS. The claim about Readability not stripping event handlers may be library-specific, but even without that, the RSS path clearly allows arbitrary attributes/tags and is rendered unsanitized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML/attribute injection: topic_embed.rb interpolates url into HTML with only a weak ^https?:// regex check, allowing crafted URLs (e.g. with ' onmouseover=') to inject raw HTML into post body, leading to stored XSS

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML snippet containing `#{url}` into `contents` with no escaping, and only gates `url` with `^https?://`. A crafted URL like `http://eviltrout.com/'onmouseover='alert(1)` still matches the regex and is also a syntactically valid URI path character set, so it will be interpolated into the single-quoted `href` attribute and can inject arbitrary attributes/HTML. This is then persisted as a post created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` (bypassing cooking/sanitization), while the embed view renders with `raw post.cooked`. That combination makes it a stored XSS vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reflected XSS: embed.html.erb interpolates client-controlled Referer header into inline JS postMessage call without escaping; ensure_embeddable only validates the host, so attacker-controlled path/query can break out of the JS string
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying vulnerability: the client-controlled Referer header is interpolated into inline JavaScript without proper escaping, enabling reflected XSS (host validation alone doesn’t prevent malicious path/query from breaking out of the JS string).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF: open-uri fetches in TopicEmbed and PollFeed follow redirects without host/scheme validation, allowing the embeddable host to redirect the server to internal addresses like 169.254.169.254
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe an SSRF risk in PollFeed caused by using open-uri to fetch a URL without sufficient validation. The golden focuses on the attacker controlling `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`; the candidate frames it as missing host/scheme validation and redirect-following (and also mentions TopicEmbed), but it still identifies the same core issue: PollFeed can be made to fetch arbitrary/internal URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weak origin check in embed.js uses substring matching (indexOf) instead of strict origin equality, potentially allowing suffix/subdomain origin matches when trusting e.data.height
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same security flaw: origin validation uses indexOf/substring matching rather than strict origin equality, allowing a malicious domain (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com) to bypass the check and be trusted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever_spec.rb:32-43 stubs retrieved_recently? and only tests dispatch, leaving real throttle logic (setnx/expire, no_throttle staff bypass) untested

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb (lines ~32-43 in the new file), the tests for the valid-host path explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called. That does mean the actual throttle implementation in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (the Redis `setnx`/`expire` behavior and the `no_throttle` bypass) is not exercised by these tests. However, this is a test-coverage gap rather than a verifiable functional bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff; the production code may still be correct even without direct unit tests for that private method’s internals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) path wired in retrieve_topic.rb:16

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` wiring in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, and the added specs cover `TopicRetriever` behavior only by stubbing `retrieved_recently?` directly; they do not exercise `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` or verify that staff users actually bypass throttling via the `no_throttle` option. However, “no test coverage” is not a verifiable correctness/security defect in the code itself—it's a testing gap/process concern rather than a concrete bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb:31-39 stubs poll_feed itself; real poll_feed body (SimpleRSS parsing, url fallback branch, CGI.unescapeHTML, user lookup, TopicEmbed.import) never executed by tests

adjudication.rationale: The spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb examples for `execute` set expectations on `poll_feed` being called or not called (e.g., `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once/never`), so the real `poll_feed` implementation (SimpleRSS parsing, user lookup, `TopicEmbed.import`, etc.) is indeed never exercised by these tests. However, this is a test-coverage critique rather than a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the diff: the tests are intentionally scoped to `execute`’s guard conditions and delegation, not to `poll_feed`’s internal behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor.rb:85 save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) behavioral change has no test passing skip_validations to revise!

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from always validating (@post.save) to conditionally skipping validations when opts[:skip_validations] is true. This is an intentional behavior extension (and is used in the same diff by TopicEmbed.import calling revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true)). The proposed finding complains there is no test specifically covering passing skip_validations to revise!, but lack of a dedicated test is not itself a verifiable defect introduced by the diff, and the default behavior (validations on) remains unchanged when skip_validations is not provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb:36-42 asserts against mocks instead of verifying Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) with correct embed_url/user_id

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it enqueues a background job: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. However, embed_controller_spec.rb (the "tells the topic retriever to work..." example around lines 36-42) sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`, which are never called by the controller. The spec also does not verify the actual behavior (that `Jobs.enqueue` is called with correct args). This is a concrete mismatch/defect in the diff (the test would fail / not test the intended behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb:39-42 never verifies content_sha1 is updated, so regression to a no-op update_column causing permanent re-revision would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s runtime code in `TopicEmbed.import` does update `content_sha1` via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` when content changes, so there is no verifiable functional bug introduced here. The proposed finding is about missing test coverage in `topic_embed_spec.rb` (it checks `post.cooked` changes but doesn’t assert the `topic_embeds.content_sha1` value changes), which is speculative (guards against a hypothetical future regression) rather than a real defect present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method migration default of 1 means raw_html, backfilling all existing posts to raw_html so cooked output silently becomes raw markdown

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. In this codebase pattern (see existing `Post.types ||= Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`), `Enum.new` typically assigns `1` to the first symbol, meaning `1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Therefore existing posts being backfilled to `1` would keep the default cooking pipeline, not switch to raw HTML. The finding’s claim that default 1 means `raw_html` and would change existing cooked output is a misread of the enum ordering and is not a verifiable problem from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostCreator never sets cook_method for new posts, so all new posts inherit DB default 1 (raw_html) and are rendered raw

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the diff. `PostCreator` *does* set `cook_method` when provided: `post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method] if @opts[:cook_method].present?` (lib/post_creator.rb). Also the migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`, but `Post.cook_methods` is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which in this codebase typically maps the first symbol to `1` and the second to `2`; so default `1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Therefore new posts will not all be rendered raw by default, and the reported issue is not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to create_table :top_topics migration will DROP TABLE and irreversibly destroy existing top_topics data on re-execution

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before (re)creating it. That means if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, manual execution, or in an environment where `top_topics` already exists), it can destroy any existing `top_topics` data rather than failing safely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds migration creates no foreign keys, allowing dangling topic_id/post_id references that break the embed route when topics/posts are deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s migration `create_topic_embeds` indeed creates `topic_id`/`post_id` integer columns without database-level foreign keys. However, whether that is a “real problem” (dangling references) and whether it “breaks the embed route” is not verifiable from this diff alone: Rails apps commonly omit DB FKs, and cleanup could be handled via application callbacks elsewhere (e.g., dependent destroys on Topic/Post) that are not shown here. The claim about the embed route breaking on deletions depends on behavior outside the diff (how deletions are handled and how `TopicView.new` behaves for missing topics).
